passages.text: Page Overview 72 Results of Operations by Registrant 73 Sempra 73 SDG&E 83 SoCalGas 86 Capital Resources and Liquidity 88 Critical Accounting Estimates 108 New Accounting Standards 112 OVERVIEW This combined MD&A includes the operational and financial results of the following three Registrants: ▪ Sempra is a holding company whose principal businesses are regulated utilities in California and Texas. Our businesses invest in and operate electric and gas utilities and other energy infrastructure that provide energy services to customers. ▪ SDG&E is a regulated public utility that provides electric service to San Diego and southern Orange counties and natural gas service to San Diego County. ▪ SoCalGas is a regulated public natural gas distribution utility, serving customers throughout most of Southern California and part of central California. Sempra has the following three reportable segments which reflect how the CODM oversees operational and financial performance: ▪ Sempra California ▪ Sempra Texas Utilities ▪ Sempra Infrastructure SDG&E and SoCalGas each have one reportable segment. Below are significant events, including major project updates, that affected our business in 2025 and may continue to affect our future results: ▪ The 2025 Wildfire Legislation was signed into law and established, among other things, an $18 billion Continuation Account that would provide additional liquidity to reimburse catastrophic wildfire-related claims incurred by large California electric IOUs if the Wildfire Fund is depleted, and a multi-stakeholder task force, coordinated by the Wildfire Fund’s administrator, to prepare and submit to the California legislature and Governor of California on or before April 1, 2026, a report that evaluates and sets forth recommendations on new models to complement or replace the Wildfire Fund ▪ The CPUC issued an FD for SDG&E’s and SoCalGas’ cost of capital for 2026 through 2028 ▪ The CPUC issued an FD in SDG&E’s 2024 GRC Track 2 request that authorizes partial recovery of SDG&E’s WMP costs ▪ Oncor filed its 2025 comprehensive base rate review and expects to receive a final order from the PUCT in the first half of 2026 ▪ In June 2025, Texas House Bill 5247, which established the UTM, was signed into law and became effective ▪ In September 2025, we entered into an agreement to sell 45% of our equity interest in SI Partners to the KKR Partners for an aggregate base purchase price of approximately $9.99 billion, subject to adjustments, and expect the sale to close in the second or third quarter of 2026, subject to closing conditions ▪ In December 2025, we entered into an agreement to sell Ecogas for 9.0 billion Mexican pesos (approximately $500 million U.S. dollar-equivalent at December 31, 2025), subject to adjustments, and expect the sale to close in the second or third quarter of 2026, subject to closing conditions ▪ We sold a 49.9% equity interest in the PA LNG Phase 2 project to Blackstone ▪ SI Partners reached a positive FID on the PA LNG Phase 2 project and issued a full notice-to-proceed under Bechtel’s fixed-price EPC contract ▪ We invested $12.6 billion in capital expenditures and investments 2025 Form 10-K | 72 Tab

passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: When evaluating our company and its businesses and any investment in our or their securities, you should carefully consider the following risk factors and all other information contained in this report and the other documents we file with the SEC (including those filed subsequent to this report). We also may be materially harmed by risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently consider immaterial. If any of these risks occur, our results of operations, financial condition, cash flows and/or prospects could be materially adversely affected, our actual results could differ materially from those expressed or implied in our forward-looking statements, and the trading prices of our securities and those of our businesses could decline. These risk factors are not prioritized in order of importance or materiality, and they should be read together with the other information in this report, including in the Consolidated Financial Statements and in “Part II – Item 7. MD&A.” RISKS RELATED TO SEMPRA Operational and Structural Risks Sempra’s ability to pay dividends and meet its obligations largely depends on the performance of its subsidiaries and entities accounted for as equity method investments. We are a holding company and substantially all the assets that produce our earnings are owned by our subsidiaries or equity method investees, which are entities we do not control. SI Partners, which primarily constitutes our Sempra Infrastructure reportable segment, will be accounted for as an equity method investment subject to closing the planned sale of 45% of our equity interest, which we expect to occur in the second or third quarter of 2026. Our ability to pay dividends and meet our debt and other obligations largely depends on distributions from our subsidiaries and equity method investees, which in turn depend on their ability to execute their business strategies and generate cash flows in excess of their own expenditures, dividend payments to third-party owners (if any) and debt and other obligations. In addition, our subsidiaries and entities accounted for as equity method investments are all separate and distinct legal entities that are not obligated to pay dividends or make loans or distributions to us and could be precluded from doing so by legislation, regulation or contractual restrictions, in times of financial distress or in other circumstances. Any inability to access capital from our subsidiaries and equity method investees could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition, cash flows and/or prospects. Sempra’s rights to the assets of its subsidiaries and equity method investees are structurally subordinated to the claims of each entity’s trade and other creditors. When Sempra is a creditor of any such entity, its rights as a creditor are effectively subordinated to any security interest in the entity’s assets and any indebtedness of the entity senior to that held by Sempra. The principal terms of Sempra’s committed line of credit include the following: ▪ The facility has a syndicate of 23 lenders. No single lender has greater than a 6 % share in the facility. ▪ The facility provides for the issuance of $ 200 million of letters of credit. Subject to obtaining commitments from existing or new lenders and satisfaction of other specified conditions, Sempra has the right to increase its letter of credit commitment to up to $ 500 million. No letters of credit were outstanding at December 31, 2025. ▪ Borrowings bear interest at a benchmark rate plus a margin that varies with Sempra’s credit rating. ▪ Sempra must maintain a ratio of indebtedness to total capitalization (as defined in its credit facility) of no more than 65 % at the end of each quarter. credit_strengths.text: Sempra's regulated utility footprint across California and Texas underpins a large, largely rate-regulated revenue base, and the operating margin sits modestly above the sector median, supporting the view that core earnings quality is sound despite the holding-company structure.

Operating cash flow covers declared dividends and buybacks comfortably, with distributions absorbing only a portion of internally generated cash, so shareholder returns are funded from operations rather than incremental borrowing at the parent level.

key_risks.text: Leverage is elevated: gross and net leverage both sit above the sector median and rose year over year, placing the issuer in the highly leveraged band. The gap to the next upgrade threshold is narrow, so modest EBITDA erosion would entrench the weaker profile.

The holding company depends on distributions from subsidiaries and equity method investees that are separate legal entities, structurally subordinated to their own creditors and able to restrict upstream payments; the planned partial sale of the infrastructure stake further reduces consolidated access to that cash flow.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is thin at roughly two times operating income and has fallen sharply year over year, now below the sector median. With interest expense a large fixed claim, coverage leaves limited cushion against rate resets on the junior subordinated notes.

Free cash flow is deeply negative because capital expenditure far exceeds operating cash flow, so the funding gap is met with debt rather than retained cash. Cash on hand is minimal relative to the debt stack, and the committed line provides only partial backup.

overall_credit_view.text: The maturity ladder is manageable near term, with modest notes due within the next twelve months and the bulk of principal extending beyond five years, but refinancing of the current portion and commercial paper depends on continued access to the committed facility and investment-grade markets.

Our judgement is a highly leveraged but stable utility profile: leverage above the sector median, coverage below peers and negative free cash flow offset by regulated cash flow visibility and a liquidity backstop. Direction is mildly negative given rising leverage and falling coverage.

credit_strengths.text: Sempra 於加州及德州的受監管公用事業版圖，支撐龐大且大部分受費率監管的收入基礎，而營業利潤率略高於行業中位數，支持核心盈利質量穩健的看法，儘管存在控股公司架構。
經營現金流可從容覆蓋已宣派股息及回購，分派僅佔內部產生現金的一部分，因此股東回報由營運資金支持，而非依賴母公司層面的新增借款。

key_risks.text: 槓桿偏高：總槓桿及淨槓桿均高於行業中位數，並按年上升，使發行人處於高槓桿區間。與下一個上調門檻的差距狹窄，因此 EBITDA 若輕微侵蝕，將鞏固較弱的狀況。
控股公司依賴附屬公司及權益法投資對象的分派，而該等實體為獨立法律實體，在結構上次於其自身債權人，並可限制向上游付款；計劃中的基礎設施權益部分出售，進一步減少對該現金流的合併層面取用。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率偏薄，約為營業收入的兩倍，並按年大幅下降，現已低於行業中位數。由於利息開支屬龐大固定索償，覆蓋率對次級票據的利率重設所提供的緩衝有限。
自由現金流嚴重為負，因資本開支遠超經營現金流，資金缺口以債務而非留存現金填補。相對債務結構，手頭現金極少，而承諾信貸額度僅提供部分備援。

overall_credit_view.text: 短期到期結構可控，未來十二個月內到期的票據金額不大，大部分本金延至五年以後，但當前部分的再融資及商業票據依賴持續取得承諾信貸額度及投資級市場准入。
我們的判斷為高槓桿但穩定的公用事業狀況：槓桿高於行業中位數、覆蓋率低於同業，以及負自由現金流，由受監管現金流的可見性及流動性後備支持所抵銷。方向略為負面，因槓桿上升及覆蓋率下降。
